title: fix(core): the fellow-org peer list keeps every member the first membership read returned
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8UqrAZsJzxmjyAzE8Z3mZR1)_

Refs #29398 (item 2)

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:组织成员数达到 1,000 时,解析器会先读一次 1,000 行、再按 id 分页读完整成员;现在两次读的结果取并集,而不是用第二次的结果替换第一次。
- 为什么改:若补全读看到的成员比第一次少(另一连接上的旧快照),同组织成员列表 `org_user_ids` 会比第一次读本身还短,这些成员在普通成员的 `sys_user` 读取里悄悄消失。
- 风险与回滚:两次读都按当前组织过滤,并集不会加入组织外的人;不增加也不改变任何读;回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` 第 5 步(`orgMembers` 的并集一行),再看同目录 `resolve-authz-context.org-members-past-first-read.test.ts` 的新用例。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run src/security/resolve-authz-context.org-members-past-first-read.test.ts`,预期 9/9 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。卡的第 1 项(按 id 顺序的逐页校验)不在本 PR,卡保持打开,见 Acceptance notes。

## What changes

`resolveUserAuthzGrants` step 5 builds `org_user_ids` from Leg 1's `sys_member` read (`orgMembersLeg`, bounded at 1,000 rows). When that read comes back at its bound, `readOrganizationMembersToCompletion` reads the whole membership in id order. Its rows used to replace `orgMembersLeg`. They are now unioned with it, so a completion that sees fewer members than Leg 1 already held cannot shorten the list. Both reads filter on the active organization, so the union adds nobody outside it. No read is added, removed or changed, and the batch-equivalence goldens do not move.

One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/core`.

## Why

This is item 2 of the card: a completion that answers from an older snapshot on another connection returned a shorter list than the first read alone. Item 1 (the per-page order check) is held back. The Acceptance notes say why.

## Tests

- New case in `resolve-authz-context.org-members-past-first-read.test.ts`: 1,005 members, and the completion's ordered reads cannot see five members the unordered first read returned. Every one of the five, and the whole membership, is still in `org_user_ids`, and nobody from the other organization is.
- The fake driver gains `staleForOrderedReads`, a set of user ids that its ordered `sys_member` reads (the completion's) do not return.

## Acceptance notes

**Item 1 of the card is held back, as the seat ruled.** The card's suggested per-page check ("each id strictly greater than the row before it") would compare ids in JavaScript code-point order. `driver-sql` emits a plain `ORDER BY id` and `id > ?`, so the database collation decides the order. The keyset itself is sound under any collation, because the cursor and the order use the same comparison. A JavaScript check would not be. Measured on a local PostgreSQL 16, sorting seven nanoid-shaped values:

- `C.UTF-8` database: `AC Ab9 B-2 a-c aB3 ab b_1`, which matches JavaScript.
- ICU `en-US` database (`CREATE DATABASE ... LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE 'en-US'`): `a-c ab aB3 Ab9 AC b_1 B-2`.

Member ids are mixed-case (nanoid in the drivers, better-auth's generator through plugin-auth). On such a database, every correctly ordered completion page would fail the check, and every request in an organization past the first read's bound would get a 503. MySQL's default `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` collation is case-insensitive and differs from code-point order in the same way (not measured here). Collation-safe designs are left on the card for a decision.
